builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Where Is the Truth When AI Agents Disagree? Dependence-Aware Belief Propagation for Unsupervised Truth Discovery (Extended Version)
summary: BP-TD replaces plain majority vote and classical Dawid-Skene crowdsourcing estimators for combining conflicting answers from multiple LLM agents by adding per-agent decorrelation weights so that agents sharing a base model count as roughly one vote. It costs only mean-field variational inference over a one-coin model, which is computationally trivial on constrained infrastructure, but it requires maintaining a multi-agent pool whose members are meaningfully diverse rather than variants of one model. It can fail when the largest correlated bloc is actually the strongest agent group, in which case decorrelation hurts accuracy, and the authors report no label-free statistic that distinguishes this case from the favorable one.
rationale: The method is cheap to implement and improves label-free aggregation over majority vote, but the gain is pool-dependent, can reverse sign, and is dominated by simply labelling 20 questions and picking the best single agent, so adoption should follow a small workload-specific validation.
technique: Dependence-aware belief propagation for unsupervised truth discovery (BP-TD)

claims.statement: BP-TD replaces plain majority vote and classical Dawid-Skene crowdsourcing estimators for combining conflicting answers from multiple LLM agents by adding per-agent decorrelation weights so that agents sharing a base model count as roughly one vote. It costs only mean-field variational inference over a one-coin model, which is computationally trivial on constrained infrastructure, but it requires maintaining a multi-agent pool whose members are meaningfully diverse rather than variants of one model. It can fail when the largest correlated bloc is actually the strongest agent group, in which case decorrelation hurts accuracy, and the authors report no label-free statistic that distinguishes this case from the favorable one.

On 13 local LLM agents on MMLU, BP-TD achieves 0.716 accuracy versus 0.624 for majority vote (160 questions) and 0.707 versus 0.674 (10,000 questions), without labels; however, with only 20 labelled questions, selecting the single best agent outperforms all tested aggregators on MMLU, ARC and TruthfulQA.
